title.narrative: Strengthening TCU Financial Audit of the Consolidated Financial Statements of the Government of Brazil

description.narrative: The key development objective of the proposed IDF is to accelerate the Tribunal de Contas da União's (TCU), the Brazilian Supreme Audit Institution (SAI), acquisition of institutional capabilities to issue an audit opinion, consistent with international standards on auditing (ISAs), or national auditing standards significantly consistent with international standards, on the consolidated financial statements of the Government of Brazil. The objective is to set the TCU on a path to emerge as a reference among SAIs in the LAC Region in the field of financial auditing on consolidated financial statements, one of the SAI's primary external control responsibilities. Moreover, the objective is to ensure that the TCU has the institutional capabilities to issue a financial audit opinion on the consolidated financial statements of the Government prepared based on the forthcoming, and first-ever, NBCASPs, the Brazilian Accounting Standards Applicable to the Public Sector, based on the International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS) issued by the International Federation of Accountants (IFAC). Without the IDF, the current evolution in TCU's financial audit capabilities may not keep pace with the revolution taking place in Brazilian public sector accounting and financial reporting. TCU's financial audit learning curve must be shortened and steepened. The TCU reports to the Legislative Branch and is the external audit organization of the government, the Brazilian Supreme Audit Institution or SAI. One of its primary responsibilities is to present a report and statement to the Congress on the yearly report prepared by Executive Branch - the Presidency. The Governmental Macro-Evaluation Secretariat (SEMAG) is the TCU technical unit responsible for preparing the audit opinion and final report, under the supervision of one of TCU´s Ministers. The TCU's current yearly report analyses important macro issues regarding the government budget planning and execution, accounting, performance of the economy and government actions. Financial auditing is carried out but planning and execution of the audits can still be significantly improved. TCU believes that there is a need to strengthen financial audit capabilities oriented towards supporting the TCU's audit opinion on the consolidated financial statements of the Government. A fundamental step is for all TCU financial audit work to fully comply with international and national audit standards and INTOSAI Financial Audit Guidelines and to incorporate international best practices from within the SAI community.
